LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). LT8D800A: same code as LT8F300C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open)
table.description: Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs open.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Closed)
table.description: Cap on the target EGR rate for a short time after a pedal tip-out (inferred), by rpm and load, TGVs closed.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Open, Multi-Injection)
table.description: Multi-injection version of the TGV-open EGR tip-out cap.

table.name: EGR Target Rate Tip-Out Limit (TGV Closed, Multi-Injection)
table.description: Multi-injection version of the TGV-closed EGR tip-out cap.

table.name: EGR Tip-Out Limit Duration
table.description: How long, by manifold pressure, the EGR tip-out cap is held after a pedal tip-out.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (Multi-Injection, TGV Closed)
table.description: Multi-injection copy of EGR Timing Advance (TGV Closed).

table.name: EGR Timing Advance (Multi-Injection, TGV Open)
table.description: Multi-injection copy of EGR Timing Advance (TGV Open).

table.name: EGR Timing Advance DAM Term (Multi-Injection, TGV Closed)
table.description:
As the EGR DAM term, with multiple injection.
Details: 0x0DD0DC (read), used while FFF8A775 bit 2 is set. Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance DAM Term (Multi-Injection, TGV Open)
table.description:
As the EGR DAM term, with multiple injection.
Details: 0x0DD0DC (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Timing Advance DAM Term Weight (Multi-Injection)
table.description:
How much of the multiple-injection DAM term applies, by DAM.
Details: 0x0DD0DC (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Modes 1/4, Default/Sport Sharp)
table.description: Main requested-torque threshold, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close (drive modes 1 and 4, the default); they reopen above the matching Exit table. Coolant and air-flow conditions also apply.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Modes 1/4, Default/Sport Sharp)
table.description: Main requested-torque threshold, by rpm, above which a TGV-close request clears (drive modes 1 and 4, the default). Keep above the Enter table.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, below which the TGVs may close in drive mode 2. The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Requested torque, by rpm, above which a TGV-close request clears in drive mode 2. Keep above TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Mode 2, Sport). The TGVs probably close at light load: requested torque must fall below the Enter table to close them and rise above the matching Exit table to reopen (with coolant and air-flow conditions).

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Offset
table.description: Offset added to every TGV torque threshold (except the start-mode pair) by rpm and an unidentified signal; 0 ft-lb means no change.

table.name: TGV IAT Threshold
table.description: Intake air temperature, by vehicle speed, below which the TGVs are kept open even when the torque, coolant and air-flow close conditions hold (the close request is replaced by a 'blocked' state that resets the close timer). Raise it to keep the TGVs open in cold air at speed.

table.name: TGV Coolant Minimum
table.description: Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions).

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter)
table.description: Air flow below which the TGVs may close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions together with torque and coolant). Raise it (with TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)) to let the TGVs close at higher air flow; once closed they reopen above the Exit value.

table.name: TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Exit)
table.description: Air flow above which a TGV-close request clears again (probably reopening the TGVs); the upper end of the hysteresis with TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter). Keep it above the Enter value.

table.name: TGV Close Delay
table.description: How long the TGV-close conditions must hold before the TGVs actually close, by vehicle speed. Longer = fewer TGV switches during brief light-load moments.

table.name: TGV Open Fraction from Position (Closing)
table.description: Converts measured TGV position into the open fraction used to blend every TGV-open / TGV-closed table (fuel, timing, AVCS) while the TGVs are closing; the blend also cannot fall faster than about 0.5 s from open to closed.

table.name: TGV Open Fraction from Position (Opening)
table.description: Converts measured TGV position into the open fraction used to blend every TGV-open / TGV-closed table (fuel, timing, AVCS) while the TGVs are opening; the blend ramps at about 1 s from closed to open unless the valves open faster.

table.name: TGV Motor Duty Compensation
table.description: Multiplier on the TGV motor drive duty by coolant and battery voltage, so the valves move reliably when cold or at low voltage.

table.name: TGV Drive Duty (Opening)
table.description: Motor duty used to drive the TGVs towards their open stop, by valve position (open meaning inferred). Leave alone unless the TGV actuators are changed.

table.name: TGV Drive Duty (Closing)
table.description: Motor duty used to drive the TGVs towards their closed stop, by valve position (closed meaning inferred). Leave alone unless the TGV actuators are changed.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Start Modes)
table.description: Requested-torque threshold for TGV closing in a start combustion mode.

table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Exit (Start Modes)
table.description: Exit threshold paired with TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Start Modes).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Other Drive Modes)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in the default drive mode (cruise meaning inferred). If you change Requested Torque tables, cruise response changes unless this is adjusted too.

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Other Drive Modes, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Default drive mode with the meter cruise option (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Drive Mode 2, Sport, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in drive mode 2 with the meter cruise option (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Pedal Equivalent (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Converts the cruise control torque request into a pedal-position equivalent by torque and rpm; while cruise is active the ECU uses the higher of this and the real pedal. Used in drive mode 3 with the meter cruise option (cruise meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. This is the standard km/h version.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. Standard mph version.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. km/h version with the meter cruise option.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. mph-meter version with the meter cruise option.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. km/h version with the meter cruise option and an untraced alternate flag.

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (mph Meter, Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. The ECU picks one of six tables by meter units (km/h or mph, inferred) and a cruise option flag from the meter. mph version with the meter cruise option and an untraced alternate flag.

table.name: Cruise Cancel Speed
table.description: Speed below which cruise control cancels (and the set speed is cleared), by meter (market) code.

table.name: Cruise Set Speed Ramp While Accelerating
table.description: How fast the cruise target speed rises, by speed, while the raise (accelerate) switch is held.

table.name: Cruise Torque Limit Offset
table.description: Torque margin by rpm that caps the cruise control torque request above a base torque value, limiting how hard cruise can drive the engine. One table edits all three copies (including the monitor copy).

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Default)
table.description: Main cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while holding speed and in all states without their own table. Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x23)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the raise (accelerate) switch (tap meaning inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xB0)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the lowering (coast) switch (tap meaning inferred).

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Catch-Up)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while the car catches up to a set speed changed by holding a switch (inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x40)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after the raise switch, while not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed. Higher = more aggressive throttle response.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach)
table.description: Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error while approaching a new set speed, until within about 3 km/h of it.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (Engage)
table.description: Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to when cruise starts controlling or returns to holding speed, by speed and acceleration.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (After Tap)
table.description: Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to after a set-speed switch tap, by speed and acceleration, so speed settles smoothly.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed from CAN Speed
table.description: Converts the CAN vehicle speed into the speed used by cruise control, per meter (market) code, as a straight line (scale and offset). The offsets probably make the set speed match the speedometer.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed Filter Weight
table.description: Smoothing weight for the vehicle speed used by cruise control, by speed error and speed. Larger = less smoothing, quicker reaction.

table.name: Cruise Excess Acceleration Threshold (Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description: With one cruise option and an alternate flag only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 0.2 s while cruise is on without pedal input, cruise ends (probably a runaway check).

table.name: Cruise Acceleration Cancel Threshold (Meter Cruise Option)
table.description: With one cruise option only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 3 s while cruise is on, cruise is cancelled and stays unavailable for the rest of the drive (probably a runaway check).

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xC0)
table.description: Cruise controller gain used in a cruise state probably linked to the lowering switch (inferred), when Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach) is not active.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Ramp-Down Rate
table.description: How fast, by vehicle speed, brake override ramps the accelerator signal down. Larger = faster torque cut when brake and accelerator overlap. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor
table.description: Lowest pedal value, by vehicle speed, that brake override ramps the accelerator signal down to. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Rate (Pedal Held)
table.description: How fast, by vehicle speed, the pedal limit is raised again after the brake is released while the driver keeps the accelerator pressed. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Time
table.description: Time, by vehicle speed, over which full pedal is restored after brake override ends (recovery ends early if the pedal is released or reached). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Brake Pressure Threshold
table.description: Brake pressure, by booster vacuum and vehicle speed, above which the brake counts as applied for brake override. Raise to make override need a firmer brake press. Used while the brake-pressure signal from the stability control unit is valid. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Delay
table.description: How long the brake must be pressed over a held accelerator, by pedal position and speed, before brake override starts cutting the pedal signal (above 7 km/h). Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: Brake Override Deceleration Threshold (No Pressure Signal)

scaling.units: ms per km/h of speed drop
ms per mph of speed drop

table.description: Deceleration needed (by pedal and speed) to confirm braking when the brake-pressure signal is not available, so brake override can still act from the brake switch. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.

table.name: VDC Torque Request Correction
table.description: Correction, by the gap between the stability control (VDC) torque request and actual engine torque, that sets how tightly the ECU limits target torque during a VDC torque reduction (VDC meaning inferred).

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Maximum
table.description: Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Manifold Threshold
table.description: Manifold-vacuum threshold, by barometric pressure, for a brake-booster vacuum model.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage (Normal)
table.description: The charging voltage the ECU aims for in normal running.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage (Battery Charged)
table.description: The charging voltage used once the ECU decides the battery is charged. Setting it to the normal target keeps the alternator charging.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage (Accessory Load)
table.description: The charging voltage used while an accessory-load request is active.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage (Adaptive) Maximum
table.description: Upper limit of the charging voltage the ECU works out itself in its adaptive mode.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage (Adaptive) Minimum
table.description: Lower limit of the charging voltage the ECU works out itself in its adaptive mode.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage Maximum
table.description: The charging target is never set above this.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage Minimum
table.description: The charging target is never set below this.

table.name: Charging Target Temperature Correction Threshold
table.description: The temperature correction only applies to charging targets at or above this voltage.

table.name: Charging Target Voltage at Start
table.description: The charging target the ECU starts from before its normal logic takes over.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant)
table.description: Radiator fan duty by coolant for an alternate (duty-based) fan control path.

table.name: Battery Capacity
table.description: Battery capacity the ECU uses to turn charge and discharge current into state of charge.

table.name: Battery Charge Efficiency (Charging)
table.description: How much of the charging current the state-of-charge estimate counts, by battery-sensor value.

table.name: Battery Charge Efficiency (Discharging)
table.description: How much of the discharge current the state-of-charge estimate counts, by battery-sensor value.

table.name: Battery State of Charge Reset Value
table.description: The state of charge the ECU assumes when its estimate is reset.

table.name: Battery Charged SOC Threshold
table.description: Above this state of charge, early in each charge cycle, the ECU decides the battery is charged and switches to the Battery Charged target voltage. Raising it makes the charge cut happen less often.

table.name: Battery Charged SOC Hysteresis
table.description: Once the battery counts as charged, the state of charge must rise this much above the threshold to stay so.

table.name: Battery Charged Check Window
table.description: How long into each charge cycle the battery-charged check is made.

table.name: Charge Cycle Length
table.description: Length of one charge-control cycle; the battery-charged decision is made again at the start of each.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Time Limit
table.description: Adaptive charging (the self-computed target) ends after this time in the cycle.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Charge Limit
table.description:
Adaptive charging also ends once this much charge has gone back into the battery (raw units).
Details: Compared with FFF81848, the integral of charging current while in mode 5 (0x1368C4, read; unit not confirmed). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, Flag A807 Set)
table.description: Radiator fan duty by coolant, used when an unidentified driving-condition flag is set.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Deadband Above
table.description:
Battery current may be this far above the target before the adaptive integral steps down.
Details: 0x137E7C, mode 5 only (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Deadband Below
table.description:
Battery current may be this far below the target before the adaptive integral steps up.
Details: 0x137E7C, mode 5 only (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Step Down
table.description:
Integral step each 40 ms pass while the battery current is above the target.
Details: 0x137E7C (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Step Up
table.description:
Integral step each 40 ms pass while the battery current is below the target.
Details: 0x137E7C (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Gain
table.description:
Converts the adaptive integral into a voltage correction (mV per count x 1000).
Details: B6FA = integral x this / 1000 mV (0x137E7C, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Maximum
table.description:
Upper clamp of the adaptive integral (counts).
Details: 0x137E7C (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Integral Minimum
table.description:
Lower clamp of the adaptive integral (counts).
Details: 0x137E7C (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, CAN 0x282 Value High)
table.description: Radiator fan duty by coolant, used when an unidentified CAN value is high.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Maximum
table.description: Largest correction the feedback integral can add.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Minimum
table.description: Largest correction the feedback integral can subtract.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (A/C, CAN 0x280 Value)
table.description: Radiator fan duty with the A/C requested, by an unidentified CAN value.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)
table.description: Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 1.0, blended with the DAM 0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Mostly equal to Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Open); keep consistent if you change the torque model.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 0)
table.description: Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 0, blended with the DAM 1.0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Close to, but somewhat lower than, the Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0) tables.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque)
table.description: Full-load air flow by rpm at Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque); a floor on the air used for the maximum-available torque the ECU sends over CAN (inferred). Raise it with a bigger turbo, or other modules see too low a torque capacity. Does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque)
table.description: Manifold pressure that Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) refers to, by rpm. Raising the boost limit raises the estimate in proportion, up to 1.25x. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow IAT Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description: Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by intake temperature ratio. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Boost Limit Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description: Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by the ratio of the current boost limit to Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque). Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.

table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate
table.description: How fast, by rpm, the engine torque reported over CAN to other modules (for example stability control) fades out at a fuel cut and returns after it. It does not change fuelling or throttle.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM
table.description: Road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.

table.name: Gear Road Speed per 1000 RPM (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate road speed per 1000 rpm for each gear, used only by the gear advice function. The values do not match the 6MT and probably belong to another transmission.

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map
table.description: Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies.

table.name: Gear Advice Downshift Maximum RPM (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate rpm limit, by gear, below which a downshift may be advised by the gear advice function.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM
table.description: Minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.

table.name: Gear Advice Upshift Minimum RPM (Alternate)
table.description: Alternate minimum rpm in the next gear up, by pedal and gear, for an upshift to be advised by the gear advice function.

table.name: MAF Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts MAF sensor voltage to airflow (g/s) in 64 fixed steps from 0 to 4.92 V; this airflow drives the ECU's air model, load and fuel. Rescale every point when fitting a bigger intake or a different MAF, and keep peak flow below the P0103 voltage limit. An internal 218 g/s cap on one copy of the airflow affects only purge, TGV, monitors and similar side functions, not fuel, load or timing.

table.name: MAP Sensor Multiplier
table.description: Gain of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. For a 3-bar or larger sensor set it to the new sensor's slope and set MAP Sensor Offset to match. The ECU's MAP value cannot go above 256 kPa absolute (about 22 psi boost at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted, so anything higher reads as 256 kPa.

table.name: MAP Sensor Offset
table.description: Offset of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, i.e. the sensor's reading extrapolated to 0 V. Set it together with MAP Sensor Multiplier when fitting a different MAP sensor. The result is still limited to 256 kPa absolute.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description: Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description: Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description: Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description: Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description: How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0107)
table.description: Sensor voltage below which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted low (P0107) and a substitute MAP is used. It works on raw voltage, so it does not change when you rescale the MAP sensor.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0108)
table.description: Sensor voltage above which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted high (P0108). Raw voltage, independent of the MAP scaling.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0103)
table.description: MAF voltage above which the MAF circuit-high code P0103 is set.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
table.description: Voltage below which the main IAT sensor is flagged as shorted (reads impossibly hot, P0112).

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0113)
table.description: Voltage above which the main IAT sensor is flagged as open (reads impossibly cold, P0113).

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
table.description: Voltage below which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0097).

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
table.description: Voltage above which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0098).

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0117)
table.description: Voltage below which the coolant sensor is flagged as shorted (P0117).

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
table.description: Voltage above which the coolant sensor is flagged as open (P0118).

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
table.description: Voltage below which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0197).

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)
table.description: Voltage above which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0198).

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage below which P0192 (circuit low) is set.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0193)
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage above which P0193 (circuit high) is set.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Zero-Pressure Voltage
table.description: Rail pressure sensor voltage that reads as zero pressure. Change it with Rail Pressure Sensor Gain only when fitting a different rail pressure sensor.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Gain
table.description: Slope of the rail pressure sensor conversion. Change it only for a different rail pressure sensor.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum
table.description: Highest rail pressure the sensor conversion can report.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Fault Value
table.description: Rail pressure the ECU assumes while the rail pressure sensor is faulted. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Multiplier
table.description: Gain of the ECU's barometric pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. This sensor is probably inside the ECU; leave alone.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Offset
table.description: Offset of the barometric pressure sensor conversion. Leave alone.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Enable
table.description: When set, the ECU uses its barometric pressure sensor. When cleared, it assumes sea-level pressure (101.3 kPa) everywhere, so altitude compensation stops working.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure High Limit
table.description: Fuel rail pressure limit for P0088 (rail pressure too high): the code trips when actual pressure exceeds this value plus a 2.5 MPa hysteresis for about 2 seconds, and also triggers fail-safe; after a trip, pressure must drop back to this value to recover. If you raise target rail pressure, keep peak actual pressure below this plus 2.5 MPa.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description: How far actual rail pressure may fall below target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0087 sets, after about 10 seconds. Raising it makes the code harder to set.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description: How far actual rail pressure may rise above target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0088 sets, after about 10 seconds. Raising it makes the code harder to set.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Low Limit
table.description: Rail pressure floor by rpm for P0087 (rail pressure too low): the code counts a fault when actual pressure stays more than 0.30 MPa (hysteresis cal) below this value for about 10 seconds, and recovers when pressure is back at this value.

table.name: Cold Start Timing Monitor Band (Coolant)
table.description: Diagnostic threshold, not a tuning table: how far final timing may exceed the cold-start spark target, by coolant, before the P050B cold-start timing monitor counts a fault. One entry edits all three copies.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1
table.description: First reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor: how much the front A/F sensor reading may swing, by rpm and load, over the 25-second test window. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. A fault also needs A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 to be exceeded. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2
table.description: Second, higher reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor, used with A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2 as confirmation. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.

table.name: EGR Enable
table.description: Master switch for EGR. Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off variants of base timing, closed loop target and throttle tables become the live ones (inferred).

table.name: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT
table.description: Tells the ECU whether it is in a manual or an AT/CVT car (clear = manual in every manual image). It decides gear calculation, the gear torque limits and whether the AT/CVT Coding table variants are used. Do not change on a manual car.

table.name: Transmission Coding: From Input Port
table.description: When set, the manual/automatic coding is read from a hardware input instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT.

table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B
table.description: Enables the second (Path B) tip-in torque shaping. Leave clear unless you calibrate the whole Path B set.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description: When set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate) probably replaces the normal open loop fueling strategy.

table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description: When set, Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready) is used while the cams are probably not yet under control.

table.name: Base Timing: Pedal-Released Tables Enable
table.description: Clear it to use the normal base timing tables off-throttle too.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 1
table.description: Allows double/triple injection while one of the high-pedal latches is set.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 2
table.description: Allows double/triple injection while a second high-pedal latch is set.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 3
table.description: Allows double/triple injection while a third high-pedal latch is set.

table.name: Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (TGV Open)
table.description: Reduces cranking fuel as cranking rpm rises, by rpm and coolant, TGVs open side of a TGV blend (255 = x1.0, inferred). Edit the TGV Closed / Open pair together.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Secondary RPM Multiplier (TGV Open)
table.description: Secondary-path copy of Cranking Fuel RPM Multiplier (TGV Open): reduces secondary cranking fuel as rpm rises. Edit the TGV Closed / Open pair together.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 2 (Restart after Key-Off)
table.description: Running-path after-start enrichment 2 by coolant for a restart after key-off (start type meaning inferred). The ECU uses the largest of the three terms, each faded by its decay table; cut at very high load. Also blocks long-term trim learning while active.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 2 (Restart after Stall)
table.description: Running-path after-start enrichment 2 by coolant for a restart after a stall (start type meaning inferred). The ECU uses the largest of the three terms, each faded by its decay table; cut at very high load. Also blocks long-term trim learning while active.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 3 (Restart after Key-Off)
table.description: Running-path after-start enrichment 3 by coolant for a restart after key-off (start type meaning inferred). The ECU uses the largest of the three terms, each faded by its decay table; cut at very high load. Also blocks long-term trim learning while active.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 3 (Restart after Stall)
table.description: Running-path after-start enrichment 3 by coolant for a restart after a stall (start type meaning inferred). The ECU uses the largest of the three terms, each faded by its decay table; cut at very high load. Also blocks long-term trim learning while active.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Special Start)
table.description: A first start (type 0) uses x1.0. Multiplier in the normal cranking pulse FFF8AFC6 when FFF8A6E7 = 3 (0x0C9038, coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50, read from the call at 0x0C6896); 255 (x1.0) for other values. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A350 by the code that reads it (read). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). LT8D800A: same code as LT8F300C; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Descriptor 06BE6C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Path B, Drive Mode 2, Sport)
table.description: Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 2 with manual coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's fast stage.

table.name: Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial)
table.description: Gain multiplier (1.0 = normal) on the ECU's manifold pressure model when manifold pressure falls quickly: the first phase, for Manifold Model Falling-MAP Initial Duration. Makes the model follow the drop faster. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
table.description: Gain multiplier (1.0 = normal) on the ECU's manifold pressure model when manifold pressure falls quickly: the recovery phase after the initial phase, until the pressure drop has settled. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
table.description: Gain multiplier (1.0 = normal) on the ECU's manifold pressure model when manifold pressure falls quickly with the TGVs closed: the recovery phase after the initial phase, until the pressure drop has settled. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, Neutral)
table.description: Gain multiplier (1.0 = normal) on the ECU's manifold pressure model when manifold pressure falls quickly in neutral: the recovery phase after the initial phase, until the pressure drop has settled. Normally leave alone.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as stopped in gear for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description: Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car.

table.name: Alternator Command from Target Voltage
table.description: Alternator control duty by target charging voltage (probably). Changing it changes the charging voltage the alternator actually reaches. Also feeds Idle Air Trim (Charging Command).

table.name: Charging Target Temperature Correction
table.description: Subtracted from the charging target (when that target is at or above the threshold): negative values raise the target. The axis is a raw value from the battery sensor, probably its temperature.

table.name: Charge Control Delay After Start (SOC, Battery Sensor)
table.description: After a start, charge control (the battery-charged decision and adaptive charging) may begin this long after the engine starts, by the estimated state of charge at start and the battery sensor value.

table.name: Charge Control Charge After Start (SOC)
table.description: Charge control may also begin once the battery has taken back this much charge since the start, by the estimated state of charge at start.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Target Current
table.description: During adaptive charging the ECU steers the charging voltage so the battery takes this current, by state of charge: positive charges, negative lets the battery discharge.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Current Gain
table.description: How strongly adaptive charging moves its voltage target to reach the target battery current.

table.name: Charging Feedback Proportional
table.description: Correction added to the charging target in proportion to how far the battery voltage is from it.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Step Up
table.description: How fast the charging-voltage feedback raises the target when the battery is below it.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Step Down
table.description: How fast the charging-voltage feedback lowers the target when the battery is above it.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Gain
table.description:
Scales the feedback integral (100 = as is).
Details: Integral x this / 100 after the clamp (0x13866C, read). Address 03FE70. Confidence: read.

table.name: Charging Feedback Deadband Above
table.description: Battery voltage may be this far above target before the integral steps down.

table.name: Charging Feedback Deadband Below
table.description: Battery voltage may be this far below target before the integral steps up.

table.name: Charging Feedback Minimum RPM
table.description: The charging-voltage feedback only runs above this engine speed.

table.name: P0299 Underboost Error Threshold
table.description: Fail count while FFF8AB1E (target - actual) >= this.

table.name: P0299 Underboost Time
table.description: LT8F300C 0x097A16 (read).

table.name: (P000A) Intake Camshaft Position Slow Response (Bank 1)
table.description: Left cell, Enabled: 1 = this code can set and report, 0 = it never sets (its monitor still runs and other logic that reads the raw result may still react). Right cell, Fail-Safe: 1 = a failed test of this code raises the fail-safe request (what that request limits is not yet decoded). Needs RomRaider 1.0.0 or later.

Right cell, Fail-Safe: 1 = a failed test of this code raises the fail-safe request (what that request limits is not yet decoded). Needs RomRaider 1.0.0 or later.

Cranking Fuel (Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
table.description:
Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat attempt in the special start type.
Coolant-indexed base of the cranking pulse FFF8AFC6 (0x0C9038, read); used when flag s4 (= TGV-module flag FFF8A881 bit 2, read) set, s8 set, FFF8A6E7 = 3 (s8 = FFF811A7 bit 7, the repeat-crank history; argument mapping read from the calls at 0x0C589C). Cranking pulse (read, 0x0C9038): FFF842C8 = clamp(base x 256 x A67E x A687 x C535 x coolant multiplier x 64 / (2^32 x 255), 0, 524280) x 0.125 (the 64 is fixed, folded into the constant 5.843592e-11; Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier 05A1FC acts only on the secondary pulse in 0x0C8A28), and the per-injector quantity is never below 10 x that (0x0D168C), in 0.8 us counts. Raw units: the factors' normalisation is not fully resolved, so change it proportionally. FFF8AFC6 feeds injectors in fuel mode 0 or 3. LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Special Start)
table.description: A first start (type 0) uses x1.0. Multiplier in the normal cranking pulse FFF8AFC6 when FFF8A6E7 = 3 (0x0C9038, coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50, read from the call at 0x0C6896); 255 (x1.0) for other values. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A350 by the code that reads it (read). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Descriptor 06C81C. Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Prime Pulse Coolant Multiplier
table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). The pulse is proportional to this value. LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 1 (Special Start)
table.description:
Running After-Start Enrichment 1 for the special start type, which is disabled by calibration.
Details: When used: start type FFF8A6E7 = 3 or above, in fuel states 2 (cranking) and 3 (running). Amount E1 (1/256 of fuel) for this start type, on coolant FFF88A44. 0x0CDD8C (read) builds FFF8B010: three amounts E1/E2/E3, each from a coolant table chosen by start type FFF8A6E7 (0 first start, 1 restart after key-off, 2 restart after stall, else special start; type and coolant FFF88A44 latched when fuel state 2/3 is entered (start of cranking, or a return from 3 to 2) for the amounts E1-E3, and latched again when fuel state 3 is entered (end of cranking) for the decay tables D1-D3), each faded linearly to zero over 8 x D passes of FFF8B06A (passes since fuel state 3, 0x0D1354) by its own decay table D1/D2/D3 (factor = clamp((8D - FFF8B06A) x 32 / D, 0, 255) / 256; no fade while cranking); FFF8B010 = max(E1, E2, E3) x 05AA60(rpm)/128 x FFF8A696/128 + Low Rail Pressure Start Enrichment, forced to 0 at load FFF8A616 >= cal 0x237C8 (255, hysteresis cal 0x237C9) and outside fuel states 2/3. FFF8B010 is summed with Warm-Up Enrichment FFF8B030 in the enrichment term of the fuel factor 0x0C558C (read), blocks long-term trim learning (0x0FFE40) and is read by the closed-loop controller 0x0FD76C. This is the running-path counterpart of After-Start Enrichment 1-3 (0x0CD834 -> FFF8B012, start path). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, Low Rail Pressure)
table.description:
Injection angle while cranking for a stop-start restart with rail pressure below 2 MPa. Stop-start cannot activate in this calibration, so probably unused. Not clamped by the ECU: keep it within 0.5-180 BTDC. Edit with the High Rail Pressure table.
Details: When used: while cranking (fuel state FFF8906B = 2) with the stop-start restart request FFF89066 bit 0 set and rail pressure FFF88884 below cal 0x2A65E (3279 = 2.0 MPa / 290 psi) (0x0CFB28, called from 0x0C589C with (906B, coolant FFF88A44, rpm/50, cal 0x38448 bit 7, FFF89066 bit 0, FFF88884, &FFF8B050, &FFF8B008), args read in the caller's disassembly). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). It replaces Start Injection Angle (Fuel Mode 0) in FFF8B050, which 0x0CB394 uses as the first-pulse angle of injectors in fuel mode 0 (segment 3, offset B050 - 1080) (read). Unlike that table it is only floored at code 0, not clamped to 1080-1439, so keep it within 180-0.5 BTDC (code 1080-1439) (read). Setting cal 0x38448 bit 7 would force cal 0x11EBC (clamped to 1080-1439) instead. FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). Edit with the High Rail Pressure table. LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, High Rail Pressure)
table.description:
Injection angle while cranking for a stop-start restart with rail pressure at or above 2 MPa. Probably unused (stop-start cannot activate). Not clamped: keep within 0.5-180 BTDC.
Details: When used: as Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, Low Rail Pressure), but with rail pressure FFF88884 at or above cal 0x2A65E (3279 = 2.0 MPa / 290 psi) (0x0CFB28, read). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). Only floored at code 0, not clamped (read): keep it within 180-0.5 BTDC (code 1080-1439). FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cranking Injection Timing (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description:
Replaces Cranking Injection Timing while cranking for a stop-start restart. Stop-start cannot activate in this calibration, so probably unused.
Details: When used: while cranking (FFF8906B = 2) with the stop-start restart request FFF89066 bit 0 set; then it replaces Cranking Injection Timing as the main injection angle FFF8B052 (0x0CFE8C, read; args read in 0x0C589C: param_5 = coolant FFF88A44, param_11 = FFF89066 bit 0). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). Clamped to code 360-1079 = 180.5-540 BTDC (read). Cal 0x38448 bit 6 would force cal 0x11FE6. FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Double Injection Split
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the first of two injections; the second gets the rest.
Details: Share of the fuel in the first of two injections (0x0D05D8 -> FFF8B068 -> FFF8A6D1, read); the second gets the rest (0x0D0D50). Limited by FFF8A6DA (read). LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LT8F300C: same code as LT8H300D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Triple Injection Split 1
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the first of three injections (the third gets what the first two leave).
Details: Share of the fuel in the first of three injections (0x0D06EC -> FFF8A6C9 -> FFF8A6D3, read); the third gets 128 minus the first two (0x0D0DC0). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Triple Injection Split 2
table.description:
Share of the fuel in the second of three injections.
Details: Share of the fuel in the second of three injections (0x0D06EC -> FFF8A6CA -> FFF8A6D4, read). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
VE table that would replace the normal TGV-blended VE while the cams are probably not yet ready.
When that bit is set, 0x11E308 uses this table instead of the Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed) / (TGV Open) blend while FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear (read). That bit is an AVCS-ready flag from 0x1050F4 that needs both cam references learned (inferred meaning). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. Normally leave alone. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
table.description:
Base intake cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path.
Base term by rpm of the intake cam 1 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 49.2-52.0 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128; B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. The OCV duty routines 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust) set duty B8DE = B366[cam] x 10 (B380 for exhaust) only when cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 is clear (read). FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

EGR Target Rate (TGV Open, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
EGR rate target by rpm and load with the TGVs open and multiple injections per cycle.
Details: When used: TGVs not closed and multi-injection active (FFF8A775 bit 1); cal 0x2F797 bit 5 clear. Base target EGR rate A818, looked up by 0x0FA10C with rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616 (read, disassembly). Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). 0 = no EGR. LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). p16 (read): second axis FFF8CD77 = (ETC throttle position FFF8A342 - 10)/4 = (ETC actual position FFF8A2B6 - 1000)/256 (0x09D58E, 0x09DAAE, 0x0A0680, 0x06AB94): a throttle-position byte, about 0.56 % per count (inferred). LT8F300C: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.description: Alternator control duty by target charging voltage (probably). Changing it changes the charging voltage the alternator actually reaches. Also feeds Idle Air Trim (Charging Command).

table.name: Charging Target Temperature Correction
table.description: Subtracted from the charging target (when that target is at or above the threshold): negative values raise the target. The axis is a raw value from the battery sensor, probably its temperature.

table.name: Charge Control Delay After Start (SOC, Battery Sensor)
table.description: After a start, charge control (the battery-charged decision and adaptive charging) may begin this long after the engine starts, by the estimated state of charge at start and the battery sensor value.

table.name: Battery State of Charge Reset Value
Charge Control Charge After Start (SOC)
table.description: Charge control may also begin once the battery has taken back this much charge since the start, by the estimated state of charge at start.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, Flag A807 Set)
Adaptive Charging Target Current
table.description: During adaptive charging the ECU steers the charging voltage so the battery takes this current, by state of charge: positive charges, negative lets the battery discharge.

table.name: Adaptive Charging Current Gain
table.description: How strongly adaptive charging moves its voltage target to reach the target battery current.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, CAN 0x282 Value High)
Charging Feedback Proportional
table.description: Correction added to the charging target in proportion to how far the battery voltage is from it.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Step Up
table.description: How fast the charging-voltage feedback raises the target when the battery is below it.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Step Down
table.description: How fast the charging-voltage feedback lowers the target when the battery is above it.

table.name: Charging Feedback Integral Gain
table.description:
Scales the feedback integral (100 = as is).
Details: Integral x this / 100 after the clamp (0x13866C, read). Address 0407F8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Charging Feedback Deadband Above
table.description: Battery voltage may be this far above target before the integral steps down.

table.name: Charging Feedback Deadband Below
table.description: Battery voltage may be this far below target before the integral steps up.

table.name: Charging Feedback Minimum RPM
table.description: The charging-voltage feedback only runs above this engine speed.

Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
Additional Enrichment A
table.description:
Extra enrichment added to the open-loop enrichment at higher coolant and lower rpm.
Details: When used: A applies when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E, B when coolant < 0x13E1A or rpm >= 0x13E0C (in between the last value is held); the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1, whose thresholds (cal 0x13E08, 0x13E14) are 65535, and both tables are zero. Source of FFF8AFE8 (0x0CAF70, with B), a term of the commanded lambda and of the fuel factor FFF8AFBC, where it is added to the open-loop enrichment (0x0C558C, read). LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment B
table.description:
Second table of the additional enrichment, used at low coolant or high rpm.
Details: When used: see Additional Enrichment A: B applies when coolant < cal 0x13E1A or rpm >= cal 0x13E0C (A when coolant >= cal 0x13E18 and rpm < cal 0x13E0E; in between the last value is held), and the whole term needs FFF8A654 bit 1. Second source table of FFF8AFE8. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Additional Enrichment Throttle Threshold
table.description:
Throttle opening above idle, by rpm, needed to enable Additional Enrichment A/B.
0x0D3BFC (from 0x0C782C, args read) sets the Additional Enrichment enable FFF8A654 bit 1 only when, among others, FFF88A3C (throttle opening above the idle opening: FFF88A3A - FFF8AFB8, 0x08015C) >= this(rpm FFF8CD54) or FFF88EDA bit 0, and rpm >= cal 0x13E08 = 65535 and coolant >= cal 0x13E14 = 65535 (or FFF88E28 bit 1), so the enable never sets (read; my research notes section 3). Once met, the threshold becomes cal 0x13E12 itself (1049 = 2.4 %), not the table value minus 1049: the code computes threshold - (threshold - 0x13E12) (0x0D3C90-0x0D3CAE, read); the rpm and coolant hysteresis cals 0x13E0A/0x13E16 work the same way. Belongs to Additional Enrichment A/B. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Fuel (Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
table.description:
Cranking fuel pulse by coolant for a repeat attempt in the special start type.
Coolant-indexed base of the cranking pulse FFF8AFC6 (0x0C9038, read); used when flag s4 (= TGV-module flag FFF8A881 bit 2, read) set, s8 set, FFF8A6E7 = 3 (s8 = FFF811A7 bit 7, the repeat-crank history; argument mapping read from the calls at 0x0C589C). Cranking pulse (read, 0x0C9038): FFF842C8 = clamp(base x 256 x A67E x A687 x C535 x coolant multiplier x 64 / (2^32 x 255), 0, 524280) x 0.125 (the 64 is fixed, folded into the constant 5.843592e-11; Cranking Fuel Secondary Low Rail Pressure Multiplier 05A1FC acts only on the secondary pulse in 0x0C8A28), and the per-injector quantity is never below 10 x that (0x0D168C), in 0.8 us counts. Raw units: the factors' normalisation is not fully resolved, so change it proportionally. FFF8AFC6 feeds injectors in fuel mode 0 or 3. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cranking Fuel (Stall Window, Repeat Attempt, Special Start)
Cranking Fuel Coolant Multiplier (Special Start)
table.description: A first start (type 0) uses x1.0. Multiplier in the normal cranking pulse FFF8AFC6 when FFF8A6E7 = 3 (0x0C9038, coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50, read from the call at 0x0C6896); 255 (x1.0) for other values. LF9F000R: located from LF75404S 05A350 by the code that reads it (read). LF9K000D: same code as LF9F000R; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Descriptor 06D59C. Confidence: inferred.

Cranking Fuel Pedal Multiplier (Special Start)
table.description:
Special-start copy of Cranking Fuel Pedal Multiplier.
Details: When used: start type FFF8A6E7 = 3. 0x0CD7E4 (read): FFF8A67E = this(accelerator FFF88A5E), updated only while rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x1CBD8 (4000 rpm). FFF8A67E is the first factor of both cranking pulses (0x0C8A28 -> FFF8AFC4, 0x0C9038 -> FFF8AFC6, read). LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Size of what appears to be a one-shot priming injection at key-on/cranking, by coolant; the pulse is proportional to it.
Details: When used: only if cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2. 0x0CD4AC (read): FFF8A67D = this(coolant FFF8CD65 = degC + 50) during key-on and cranking (fuel state 1/2), held afterwards. 0x0CD500 / 0x0CD5DC compute the pulses FFF8C040 / FFF8C044 = 05A8F4 / 05A908(rail pressure FFF89266, FFF8A652) x flow compensation FFF8AFEA x barometric factor FFF8A687 x FFF8A67D x 2^-18 x 1.25 + latency, and 0x1D296C fires each of them once per injector (flags FFF8C6F4-C6F7) when cal 0x28D98 = 1 or 2 (read): a one-shot priming injection at start (inferred). table.name: Running After-Start Enrichment 1 (Special Start)
table.description:
Running After-Start Enrichment 1 for the special start type, which is disabled by calibration.

table.name: Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, Low Rail Pressure)
table.description:
Injection angle while cranking for a stop-start restart with rail pressure below 2 MPa. Stop-start cannot activate in this calibration, so probably unused. Not clamped by the ECU: keep it within 0.5-180 BTDC. Edit with the High Rail Pressure table.
Details: When used: while cranking (fuel state FFF8906B = 2) with the stop-start restart request FFF89066 bit 0 set and rail pressure FFF88884 below cal 0x2A65E (3279 = 2.0 MPa / 290 psi) (0x0CFB28, called from 0x0C589C with (906B, coolant FFF88A44, rpm/50, cal 0x38448 bit 7, FFF89066 bit 0, FFF88884, &FFF8B050, &FFF8B008), args read in the caller's disassembly). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). It replaces Start Injection Angle (Fuel Mode 0) in FFF8B050, which 0x0CB394 uses as the first-pulse angle of injectors in fuel mode 0 (segment 3, offset B050 - 1080) (read). Unlike that table it is only floored at code 0, not clamped to 1080-1439, so keep it within 180-0.5 BTDC (code 1080-1439) (read). Setting cal 0x38448 bit 7 would force cal 0x11EBC (clamped to 1080-1439) instead. FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). Edit with the High Rail Pressure table. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Injection angle while cranking for a stop-start restart with rail pressure at or above 2 MPa. Probably unused (stop-start cannot activate). Not clamped: keep within 0.5-180 BTDC.
Details: When used: as Start Injection Angle (Stop-Start Restart, Low Rail Pressure), but with rail pressure FFF88884 at or above cal 0x2A65E (3279 = 2.0 MPa / 290 psi) (0x0CFB28, read). Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). Only floored at code 0, not clamped (read): keep it within 180-0.5 BTDC (code 1080-1439). FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cranking Injection Timing (Stop-Start Restart)
table.description:

Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (720 - code/2; larger = earlier), same scale as every injection-angle table (my research notes). Clamped to code 360-1079 = 180.5-540 BTDC (read). Cal 0x38448 bit 6 would force cal 0x11FE6. FFF89066 bit 0 = CAN 0x15A byte 2 bit 0, the restart request of the engine stop-start feature (signals_rates_can.md, my research notes, read). Timing added or removed according to how fast engine speed is changing, which looks like an rpm-oscillation (surge) damper.
0x0DB888 (called from 0x0DF0B8 with FFF8AA85 bit 1 and FFF8A8A1 bit 7, read): while FFF8AA85 bit 1 is set (set by 0x07FA1A when the surge damping trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear, the request is not being shaped (FFF8AEC2 <= FFF8AEBE), FFF8CEC1 bits 0-4 (rpm and load window flags) are set, speed >= cal 0x57576, gear FFF8A621 within cals 0x57577..0x57578, and FFF886AB bit 7 or FFF8A88F), FFF8A757 = clamp((this(FFF88CA4) + cal 0x2FEDE (s8 -3) x (rpm k passes ago - filtered rpm k passes ago) >> 7) x 100 >> 8, cal 0x2FEDD.. cal 0x2FEDC); k = 05B784/05B790(gear FFF8A621) + 1 (both all 0, so k = 1); rpm history FFF88CAC.. and the filtered-rpm history FFF88CC8.. (FFF8CE9A, a second lag of FFF8CEB2) (read). A757 is added to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600, read). FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold
table.description:
By DAM: a fine-knock-learning cell is counted when its learned value is at or above this, and the count sets an internal flag.
0x0E7DF8 (read): one cell per pass, it counts the FLKC cells whose flag FFF811AF[cell] is 1 and whose learned value FFF81414[cell] is at or above this(DAM FFF811AE); after all 35 cells the count goes to FFF8A792 and FFF8A7A3 bit 1 = count >= cal 0x1C699 (4). 0x0E7D0C (read) uses that bit only together with DAM inside cal 0x1C698..0x1C697 (32..48 in DAM x 16 units), which DAM (0..16) never reaches. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. 32 = no change.
Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. Normally leave alone. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path)
table.description:
Base intake cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path.
Base term by rpm of the intake cam 1 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 49.2-52.0 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128; B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. The OCV duty routines 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust) set duty B8DE = B366[cam] x 10 (B380 for exhaust) only when cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 is clear (read). FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

Idle Target Ramp Rate (AT/CVT, Mode 4 to 6)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 4 (cold idle) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 4 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration; it also needs idle mode 4. p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: read.

Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 6 -> 4. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (similarity port (code)). Confidence: read.

Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4 with the TGVs commanded closed.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Confidence: read.

EGR Target Rate (TGV Open, Multi-Injection)
table.description:
EGR rate target by rpm and load with the TGVs open and multiple injections per cycle.
Details: When used: TGVs not closed and multi-injection active (FFF8A775 bit 1); cal 0x2F797 bit 5 clear. Base target EGR rate A818, looked up by 0x0FA10C with rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616 (read, disassembly). Target EGR rate (0x0FA260, read): FFF8A81A = base A817 x Coolant Multiplier 05CB04/255 x 255/255 (A816) x Reduction Multiplier A81C/255 x DAM Multiplier 05CB10/128, x 640 (1/640 units), capped at cal 0x2C4E6 (192 = 30 %) and forced to 0 unless the enable conditions FFF8A811 bit 0 hold (0x0FAAFC). A817 follows the base table A818 (0x0FA068). Multi-injection = FFF8A775 bit 1, set by 0x0FAABC when the multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 is set and all four per-injector strategy bytes FFF8A69F..A6A2 are 2 or 3 (read). TGVs closed = FFF8A881 bit 4 set (read: 0x10C948 drives the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 to 0 while the bit is set). EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). 0 = no EGR. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.

Details: When used: only when cal 0x2F797 bit 5 is set. LT8H300D: same code as LF9K000D; address from the same instruction (exact (1 reads)). Confidence: inferred.
